note: Every case is a merged pull request of this repository, with one defect seeded into the diff. The seeding rules and the reason for the design are in README.md. Fetch the pull request head refs before a run: git fetch origin "+refs/pull/*/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr/*".

cases.title: fix(destructive-guard): v1.1 — three matcher and verdict defects
cases.head: 56bb9194e9a7e185f3928a50a16e473f3edfd538
cases.defect_description: The subcommand test is inverted. The short flag -n means --no-verify for `git commit` only, but the seeded line binds it to `git push`, where -n means --dry-run. So `git commit -n` is no longer scored and `git push -n` is scored wrongly. The two tests added in the same diff assert the opposite behaviour.

cases.title: loops: add a statistical confidence gate for benchmark-driven loops
cases.head: 1502fe72e3f3829bdb49f354fa93c0abb7e268a3
cases.defect_description: An off-by-one on the run floor. The module docstring says the rule needs three or more prior runs, and the evaluate docstring says fewer than three yields insufficient_runs. The seeded comparison also rejects exactly three runs, so the documented floor and the code disagree.

cases.title: fix(staging-guard): v1.2 — `git stage` and combined short flags bypassed v1.0
cases.head: 5e62c9f6ce9674e111cd9744377c891b3b2241fe
cases.defect_description: A weakened assertion. The test claims to prove that `git add -Au` is blocked, but the seeded assertion only checks that the helper returned something. It passes for a BLOCK verdict and for an ALLOW verdict, so the headline bypass this pull request closes is no longer covered by a test.

cases.title: fix(guard): v2.13 — an `=`-attached dest flag ate the credential source
cases.head: 2fbfee2fbe861d87aa78b3b48dafc1077f6ea574
cases.defect_description: The source half of the fix takes the wrong side of the split. It appends the flag NAME instead of the flag VALUE, so an `=`-attached source flag loses the file it names. The pull request claims to fix both the destination and the source parser; only the destination half works.

cases.title: scripts: reconcile an agent's claims against the system of record
cases.head: 52351bd23ee07e20c1411bde6d9253aad4c4a672
cases.defect_description: An unchecked None. parse_timestamp returns None for an absent or unreadable merged_at, and the function's own docstring says such a row is dropped. The seeded comparison drops the None check, so an open pull request raises TypeError and the whole snapshot fails.

cases.title: fix(config-guard): v1.2 — enumerate the two ADR-015 guards
cases.head: 5b3e16449d157c80a0e7b4ea947de8a496be0409
cases.defect_description: A weakened assertion. The new test claims that every guard in the enumeration is load-bearing on its own, but the seeded assertion only checks that the guard printed something. It passes whether the guard blocked or allowed, so the test proves nothing.

cases.title: Register hook-tamper-guard in REQUIRED_GUARDS (config-change-guard v1.3)
cases.head: 0a3cf71bfde90907e59b48fa8bb291d8b846a66b
cases.defect_description: An unrequested second entry rides in on the same line. The pull request asks only for hook-tamper-guard. The seeded line also re-declares fanout-guard, and because a later duplicate key wins in a Python dict literal, it silently moves fanout-guard from PreToolUse to the non-blocking PostToolUse event.

cases.title: fix(guard): v2.12 — a remote resource is not a local credential store
cases.head: b57d4224a9b56c9d321459bc3417632072ef9cf2
cases.defect_description: The start anchor is missing from the remote-URL pattern. The comment beside the use site says an http(s) URL is a remote resource, which means a value that IS a URL. Without the anchor any value that merely CONTAINS an http(s) substring is exempted, so a local credential path with a URL appended to it skips the sensitive-path check.

cases.title: scripts: measure rule adherence over local transcripts (v1)
cases.head: c6ec13ec8541fe8122d43bb1e05b553b4f0af85e
cases.defect_description: An off-by-one on the segment floor. The function docstring says three or more segments, and states that two-segment chains are excluded on purpose because counting them would drown the signal. The seeded comparison admits two-segment chains.

cases.title: fix(pi): close three lane gaps — shadow adapter, exact-match park, fail-open shell hedge
cases.head: 3ea7797d1edb1cc70255da31b527a740ee08fa10
cases.defect_description: The wrong end of the string is tested. The constant is named _ALLOWED_PROVIDER_PREFIX and the comment above it calls this a family match, but the seeded line tests the suffix. The documented target provider id kimi-coding starts with kimi and does not end with it, so the park check fails on its own runbook end state.
